words.gloss: in its own place, just so

hindi: वैसे ही यहाँ दोष अपने-अपने स्थान पर ही रहते हैं।
english: So here the doṣas remain just in their own places.

text_flags.why: possible: tathā + iha normally gives tatheha; the printed Devanagari (तथािह) is also malformed, so an OCR/print slip is likely; words keep tathā + iha

notes: Sentence begins with tathā 'so, likewise', so it continues an earlier statement (not in this chunk). yathāsthānam = 'according to place', i.e. each in its own place; doṣa kept (no modern equivalent).

words.gloss: one who has obtained a foetus
the puṃsavana (rite for a male child) and the like

hindi: और इसे गर्भ प्राप्त किए हुए जानकर, अनुमानित पाठ पर गर्भ के प्रकट होने से पहले, पुष्य नक्षत्र में पुंसवन आदि का प्रयोग करे।
english: And having known her to have obtained a foetus, on a conjectural reading before the foetus becomes manifest, one should employ the puṃsavana (rite for obtaining a male child) and the like in Puṣya (the lunar mansion Puṣya).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ṛrbhasya' is not a word; ga lost, ṛ stray, and garbhasya fits the sense; 'avyaktī-' also doubtful: 'before becoming unmanifest' makes no sense here, while 'before becoming manifest' agrees with unit 162 (pūrvaṃ vyakteḥ); the a- may be a doubled vowel from 'prāg'

notes: The printed token is damaged in two places (ṛrbhasya, avyaktī-); the translation adopts garbhasya and 'becoming manifest' on a conjectural reading, supported by unit 162. The subject of prayuñjīta is not stated. puṃsavana = rite performed to obtain a male child (standard); the text here names it only as 'puṃsavana and the like'. Puṣya = lunar mansion (nakṣatra) Puṣya (standard).
lines_deva: लब्धगर्भांचैनां विदित्वा प्रागव्यक्तीभावादृर्भस्य पुष्ये पुंसवनादि प्रयुंजीत
lines_iast: labdhagarbhāṃcaināṃ viditvā prāgavyaktībhāvādṛrbhasya puṣye puṃsavanādi prayuṃjīta

hindi: बारह रात्रि का काल, ऐसा अन्य लोग।
english: 'Twelve nights', so others.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'say/hold' is carried (not supplied); it gives another opinion on the time for the rite of 131. No verb supplied in the translation.

hindi: उसमें भी युग्म दिनों में, ऐसा कुछ लोग।
english: Even in that, on the paired (even) days, so some.
notes: Elliptical like 132 (verb of saying carried). yugma = paired/even; which days are meant is not stated.

hindi: प्रतिदिन, ऐसा दूसरे लोग।
english: 'Every day', so others.
notes: Elliptical, as 132-133.

hindi: वह इस प्रकार है।
english: That is as follows.
notes: Introduces the procedure of 136ff. (tadyathā = 'namely').

words.gloss: lakṣmaṇā (a plant; probably Ipomoea sepiaria; disputed); vaṭa-śuṅga (banyan shoot; Ficus benghalensis; standard); sahadevā (probably Vernonia cinerea; probable); viśvedevā (a plant name, printed viśvede-; unclear, perhaps viśvadevā; unidentified)

hindi: लक्ष्मणा, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, वट यानी बरगद के अंकुर, सहदेवा यानी सम्भवतः सहदेई और विश्वेदेवा, जो अस्पष्ट है, इनमें से किसी एक को दूध में कूटकर, अनुमानित पाठ पर पुत्र की इच्छुक होकर, दाहिने नासिकाछिद्र में तीन या चार बूँदें स्वयं डाले, और बाएँ में तो पुत्री की इच्छुक होकर।
english: Having pressed (pounded) in milk any one of lakṣmaṇā (identity disputed), vaṭaśuṅga (banyan shoots), sahadevā (probably Vernonia cinerea) and viśvedevā (unclear), she should herself instil three or four drops in the right nostril, on a conjectural reading as one desiring a son (the printed 'pitrunā' is unclear), and in the left, however, as one desiring a daughter.

text_flags.why: possible: 'pitrunā' is not a usable word here; the contrast with 'vāme tu duhitṛkāmā' makes 'putrakāmā' (desiring a son) the likely sense for the right nostril
possible: 'viśvedevānām' may be 'viśvadevānām' (a plant name); uncertain

notes: Right nostril for a son and left for a daughter is the evident contrast, but 'pitrunā' is damaged and is not built on: the translation marks a conjectural reading. The woman is the subject (duhitṛkāmā is feminine). Identifications: lakṣmaṇā disputed (commonly taken as Ipomoea sepiaria); vaṭaśuṅga = banyan shoots/buds, Ficus benghalensis (standard); sahadevā probable Vernonia cinerea (Hindi sahadevī); viśvedevā unidentified. abhiṣutya = 'having pressed/pounded'. In the Hindi, 'पहचान विवादित' refers to lakṣmaṇā.
lines_deva: लक्ष्मणावटशुंगसहदेवाविश्वेदेवानामन्यतमांक्षीरेऽभिषुत्य त्रींश्चतुरो वा बिंदून् दक्षिणे नासापुटे स्वयमासिंचेत्पित्रुना वामे तु दुहितृकामा
lines_iast: lakṣmaṇāvaṭaśuṃgasahadevāviśvedevānāmanyatamāṃkṣīre'bhiṣutya trīṃścaturo vā biṃdūn dakṣiṇe nāsāpuṭe svayamāsiṃcetpitrunā vāme tu duhitṛkāmā

hindi: और इन्हें थूके नहीं।
english: And she should not spit these out.
notes: etān (masc. plural) most likely refers to the drops (bindūn) of 136; the subject is the woman.

words.gloss: of white bṛhatī (Solanum; white form, identity disputed)

hindi: वैसे ही पुष्य नक्षत्र में उखाड़ी हुई श्वेत बृहती यानी सम्भवतः सफेद बड़ी कटेरी, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, की जड़ की लुगदी से रस नाक में डाले।
english: Likewise, from the paste of the root of white bṛhatī (a Solanum; the white form, identity disputed), uprooted under Puṣya, one should instil the juice into the nose.
notes: Subject not stated (the woman of 136). bṛhatī in general = Solanum indicum (probable); śveta-bṛhatī (white) is disputed. nāvayet = instil through the nose (nasya); the verb is causative-like, 'cause to enter the nose'. The part uprooted (root) and the process (paste, then juice) are as stated; no quantity given. Review: the subject of nāvayet is not stated (136 has svayam 'herself', 142 may point to another person instilling), so the translation says 'one'.

words.gloss: leaf (petal) of utpala (blue water lily, Nymphaea; probable)
leaf (petal) of kumuda (night water lily, Nymphaea; probable)

hindi: वैसे ही उत्पल यानी सम्भवतः नीले कमल का पत्र, कुमुद यानी सम्भवतः रात में खिलने वाले श्वेत कमल का पत्र, लक्ष्मणा की जड़ और आठ वट के अंकुर, और नाक में डाले।
english: Likewise, a leaf (petal) of utpala (probably blue water lily), a leaf (petal) of kumuda (probably night water lily), the root of lakṣmaṇā, and eight banyan shoots; and one should instil into the nose.

text_flags.why: possible: t+ca should give 'tadvacca'; one c lost before 'ut-'

notes: Elliptical: no object of nāvayet and no preparation is stated; by parity with 138 (juice from paste) something prepared from these is presumably instilled, but the text does not say so, and nothing is supplied. 'eight' is read with vaṭaśuṅgāni (the printed order 'vaṭaśuṃgāni cāṣṭau ca' is not fully clear). patra = leaf; for lotus plants also 'petal'. Identification: utpala and kumuda are both water lilies/lotuses (probable, not firm).
lines_deva: तद्वचोत्पलपत्रं कुमुदपत्रं लक्ष्मणामूलं वटशुंगानि चाष्टौ च नावयेत्
lines_iast: tadvacotpalapatraṃ kumudapatraṃ lakṣmaṇāmūlaṃ vaṭaśuṃgāni cāṣṭau ca nāvayet

words.gloss: of the measure of an udumbara (fig fruit, Ficus racemosa; standard)

hindi: और श्वेत माला और वस्त्र पहनने वाली स्त्री पुष्य नक्षत्र में उखाड़ी हुई लक्ष्मणा की जड़ की लुगदी, उदुम्बर यानी गूलर के बराबर मात्रा में, दूध के साथ पिए, पुत्र की उत्पत्ति और स्थिति के लिए।
english: And a woman wearing white garlands and garments should drink with milk a root-paste of lakṣmaṇā uprooted under Puṣya, of the measure of an udumbara (cluster fig, Ficus racemosa), for the birth and the stability of a son.
notes: udumbara-mātra = 'as much as an udumbara', used as a measure; udumbara = Ficus racemosa, cluster fig (standard); whether it is the fruit's size is the usual reading, but the text says only 'measure of an udumbara'. Hindi 'गूलर' is the ordinary name. payas can mean milk or water; milk is taken here (consistent with 136).
lines_deva: शुक्लमाल्यांबरधरा च नारी पुष्योद्धृताया लक्ष्मणाया मूलकल्कमुदुंबरमात्रंपयसा पिबेत्पुत्रस्योत्पादाय स्थितये च
lines_iast: śuklamālyāṃbaradharā ca nārī puṣyoddhṛtāyā lakṣmaṇāyā mūlakalkamuduṃbaramātraṃpayasā pibetputrasyotpādāya sthitaye ca

words.gloss: jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka (two drug names; identity disputed)

hindi: वैसे ही वौरदण्ड, जो अस्पष्ट शब्द है, अपामार्ग यानी चिचड़ा, जीवक और ऋषभक, जिनकी पहचान विवादित है, शंखपुष्पी यानी सम्भवतः शंखाहुली, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, मध्य दण्ड, सहचर यानी सम्भवतः कटसरैया, नम्रजीव, जो अस्पष्ट शब्द है, अग्निजिह्वा यानी सम्भवतः कलिहारी, या आठ वट के अंकुर।
english: Likewise: vauradaṇḍa (unclear), apāmārga (prickly chaff-flower), jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka (identities disputed), śaṅkhapuṣpī (commonly Convolvulus pluricaulis; identity disputed), a middle stalk, sahacara (probably Barleria prionitis), namrajīva (unclear), agnijihvā (probably Gloriosa superba, flame lily), or eight banyan shoots.

text_flags.why: possible: stray t after agni; agnijihvā is the plant name
possible: dittography of vā; one vā ('or eight banyan shoots') fits the sense

notes: A list of drugs; no verb or preparation is stated (the verb is carried from the surrounding unit). 'vauradaṇḍa' and 'namrajīva' are unclear in print and are neither split nor identified (vaura- might be an orthographic variant of a word beginning ba-/va-, not decided). jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka: two drug names whose botanical identity is disputed (they are generally replaced by substitutes); not identified here. madhyadaṇḍa: 'middle stalk' is the plain meaning; whether it belongs to the preceding śaṅkhapuṣpī is not decided. apāmārga = Achyranthes aspera (standard; Hindi चिचड़ा); sahacara and agnijihvā are probable only; śaṅkhapuṣpī disputed (also Evolvulus alsinoides, Clitoria ternatea are proposed). 'aṣṭau vā ... vaṭaśuṅgāni' = 'or eight banyan shoots'. Review: jīvaka and ṛṣabhaka are standard members of the aṣṭavarga group and of Caraka's jīvanīya group; usually identified as Malaxis acuminata and Malaxis muscifera respectively (disputed; the true plants are rarely available and substitutes are used).
lines_deva: तद्वद्वौरदंडमपामार्गं जीवकऋषभकौ शंखपुष्पीं मध्यदंडं सहचरं नम्रजीवमग्नित्जिह्वामष्टौ वावा वटशुंगानि
lines_iast: tadvadvauradaṃḍamapāmārgaṃ jīvakaṛṣabhakau śaṃkhapuṣpīṃ madhyadaṃḍaṃ sahacaraṃ namrajīvamagnitjihvāmaṣṭau vāvā vaṭaśuṃgāni

words.gram: pres. part. pass. √pac, n. gen. sg.

hindi: और जो पीसा हुआ है और पक रहा है, उसकी भाप सूँघकर, उसके रस को देहली पर खड़ी हुई को पहले की तरह नाक में डाले।
english: And, having smelled the vapour of what is ground and being cooked, one should instil its juice into (her) standing on the threshold, as before.
notes: Elliptical: what is ground is not named (the drugs of 141). The subject of 'having smelled' is not stated and the text does not say who smells the vapour (the woman or the person instilling); sthitām (feminine accusative) points to the woman standing on the threshold. 'as before' refers to the instillation of 136ff. 'dehalī' = threshold.
lines_deva: पिष्टस्य च पच्यमानस्योष्माणमाघ्राय तद्रसं देहल्यां स्थितां पूर्ववन्नावयेत्
lines_iast: piṣṭasya ca pacyamānasyoṣmāṇamāghrāya tadrasaṃ dehalyāṃ sthitāṃ pūrvavannāvayet

hindi: और जो कुछ और भी ब्राह्मण या वृद्ध स्त्रियाँ कहें, वह भी करे।
english: And whatever else also the brāhmaṇas or old women may say, that too she should do.
notes: The subject of kuryāt is not stated (the woman of the previous units). Nothing is added about what they may say.

hindi: फिर प्रजास्थापन नामक महा औषधियों को सिर से और दाहिने हाथ से धारण करे।
english: Then she should bear the great herbs called prajāsthāpana (offspring-establishing) with the head and with the right hand.

text_flags.why: possible: stray r after -nā; the final -ā is regular sandhi for -āḥ before m- (agreeing with mahauṣadhīḥ) and is kept

notes: The herbs of the prajāsthāpana group are not listed in this unit. The instruments 'śirasā' and 'pāṇinā' are instrumentals; the plain meaning is carrying on the head and holding in the right hand. 'oṣadhī' (f.) = herb. Review: in Caraka (Sūtrasthāna 4) prajāsthāpana is a named group of ten drugs; this text names only the group here and does not list its members, so none is identified.
lines_deva: ततः प्रजास्थापनारख्या महौषधीः शिरसा दक्षिणेन च पाणिना धारयेत
lines_iast: tataḥ prajāsthāpanārakhyā mahauṣadhīḥ śirasā dakṣiṇena ca pāṇinā dhārayeta

hindi: और इनके साथ पकाया हुआ दूध या घी पिए।
english: And she should drink milk or ghee cooked with these.
notes: siddha = cooked. 'these' are the herbs of 144. payas can also mean water; milk taken as in 140.
lines_deva: एताभिश्च सिद्धं पयो घृतं वा पिबेत्
lines_iast: etābhiśca siddhaṃ payo ghṛtaṃ vā pibet

hindi: इन्हीं से हर पुष्य में स्नान करे, और सदा इसी प्रकार स्पर्श करे।
english: With these very herbs she should bathe on every Puṣya, and she should always touch in this way.
notes: puṣye puṣye = on each occurrence of Puṣya (the lunar mansion). 'sadā' is read with ālabheta ('always in this way'); it could also go with snāyāt. ālabheta (ā-√labh) = touch, take hold of; 'them' (the herbs) is understood and not stated; it may also be read as 'apply'.

hindi: वैसे ही सब जीवनीय औषधियों का सदा प्रयोग उन-उन विधियों से
english: Likewise, the constant use of all the life-promoting (jīvanīya) herbs, by those various methods

text_flags.why: possible: with the 'ti' that opens 148 read as (i)ti, sandhi gives vidhibhir iti; 'ri' lost at the line break (words give the dictionary form vidhibhiḥ)

notes: GROUPING: the sentence appears to continue in unit 148 (which begins with a stray 'ti', probably 'iti'); the line break falls inside 'vidhibhi|ti'. No verb is stated. jīvanīya = 'life-promoting', the name of a group of herbs; its members are not listed here. Review: jīvanīya is a named group of ten drugs in Caraka (Sūtrasthāna 4: jīvaka, ṛṣabhaka, medā, mahāmedā, kākolī, kṣīrakākolī, mudgaparṇī, māṣaparṇī, jīvantī, madhuka); this text does not list its members here.

hindi: इस प्रकार गर्भ को स्थिर करने वाले।
english: Thus, the foetus-establishing (ones).

text_flags.why: possible: initial i lost; 'ti' is read as 'iti' closing the list of 147

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete/continue 147 (a closing iti and a summing-up adjective: 'these are foetus-establishing (ones)'). No noun is stated for sthāpanāni; the neuter plural adjective is shown as '(ones)'.

words.gloss: gentle in form, speech, service and conduct
following what is dear and beneficial

hindi: सौम्य आकृति, वचन, सेवा और चेष्टाओं वाले और प्रिय तथा हितकर का अनुसरण करने वाले परिचारक, और वैसे ही पति।
english: Attendants gentle in form, speech, service and conduct, and following what is dear and beneficial, and likewise the husband.
notes: No verb is stated (elliptical). It is not decided whether the adjectives also apply to the husband. The closing iti is not translated. upacāra = service/attendance; ceṣṭā = action/behaviour.

hindi: और फिर एक महीने बाद इसके पास जाए।
english: And again, after a month, he should approach her.
notes: Subject not stated; the third-person verb is read as the husband of 149. māsāt (ablative) = 'after a month' or 'from a month (onward)'. upeyāt = approach (here as a husband to his wife).

hindi: वहाँ प्रत्येक शुक्र यानी प्रजनन द्रव में, घृतमण्ड जैसा होने पर या, गर्भ की गौरता; तेल जैसा होने पर कालापन; शहद जैसा होने पर साँवलापन।
english: There, in each śukra (reproductive fluid): when it resembles ghee-maṇḍa, or, fairness of the foetus; when it resembles oil, darkness; when it resembles honey, dusky colour.
notes: Elliptical (no verb). 'śukre śukre' is read as 'in each case of śukra' (the repetition is distributive); 'vā' after the first colour is unexplained (perhaps 'or' marking alternative forms); not decided. ghṛtamaṇḍa is rendered literally as 'ghee-maṇḍa' (the clear upper part of ghee, or ghee-cream, is the usual sense, not asserted). śukra = semen (standard). Colour words: gaura fair, kṛṣṇa dark, śyāma dusky. Review: whose śukra is meant is not stated; 167 applies śukra to women as well, so the translation uses 'reproductive fluid' as in 167.
lines_deva: तत्र शुक्रे शुक्रे घृतमंदाभे वा गर्भस्य गौरत्वं तैलाभे कृष्णत्वं मध्वाभे श्यामत्वं
lines_iast: tatra śukre śukre ghṛtamaṃdābhe vā garbhasya gauratvaṃ tailābhe kṛṣṇatvaṃ madhvābhe śyāmatvaṃ

hindi: वैसे ही माता द्वारा दूध आदि मधुरों के सेवन से और जल में विहार से गौरता; अनुमानित पाठ पर तिल-अन्न और विदाही के सेवन से कालापन; मिले-जुलों के सेवन से साँवलापन।
english: Likewise, from the mother's use of sweet (ones) beginning with milk, and from her sport in water, fairness; on a conjectural reading, from (the use) of sesame-food and burning-causing (ones), darkness; from (the use) of mixed (ones), dusky colour.

text_flags.why: possible: t+m gives n (upayogān mātur); printed m
possible: the other two causes are genitive plural governing upayogāt; -ino is not a regular form before k, so -nām is likely; reading uncertain
certain spelling variant: doubled t, normalised (compare śyāmatā in 154)

notes: 'upayogāt' is carried to the second and third causes (not stated there). tilānna may be one member 'sesame-food' or two ('sesame, food'); vidāhin = causing burning (a standard term for foods that cause burning); the 'on a conjectural reading' mark covers the damaged ending. 'mother' governs both the use of foods and sport in water.
lines_deva: तथा क्षीरादिमधुराणामुपयोगाम्मातुरुदकविहाराच्च गौरता तिलांन्नविदाहिनो कृष्णता व्यामिश्राणां श्यामत्ता
lines_iast: tathā kṣīrādimadhurāṇāmupayogāmmāturudakavihārācca gauratā tilāṃnnavidāhino kṛṣṇatā vyāmiśrāṇāṃ śyāmattā

words.gloss: by conformity to country and family

hindi: और देश तथा कुल के अनुवर्तन से रंग का भेद।
english: And, by conformity to country and family, difference of colour.
notes: Elliptical (no verb). varṇa = colour (of the skin); not 'caste' here, since the preceding units speak of fair, dark and dusky.

words.gloss: from contact with the water and space elements
from contact with earth and air
in the balance of all the elements

hindi: वैसे ही तेजस् धातु के जल और आकाश धातु से संपर्क से गौरता; पृथ्वी और वायु के संपर्क से कालापन; सब धातुओं की समता में साँवलापन।
english: Likewise, from the contact of the fire element (tejas-dhātu) with the water and space elements, fairness; from contact with earth and air, darkness; when all the elements are in balance, dusky colour.
notes: dhātu here = element (the great elements: fire, water, space, earth, air), not the bodily tissue dhātu. 'of it' in the second clause (the fire element) is understood from the first clause and not stated; the text says only 'from contact with earth and air'. Elliptical (no verb).
lines_deva: तथा तेजोधातोरुदकाकाशधातुसंपर्काद्गौरता भूवायुसंपर्कात् कृष्णता सर्वधातुसाम्ये श्यामता
lines_iast: tathā tejodhātorudakākāśadhātusaṃparkādgauratā bhūvāyusaṃparkāt kṛṣṇatā sarvadhātusāmye śyāmatā

words.gloss: bringing about special features of sattva (mind)
the sattva of mother and father

hindi: सत्त्व यानी मन में विशेषता लाने वाले, फिर माता और पिता का सत्त्व, गर्भवती के बार-बार श्रवण, अपना संचित कर्म होता है, और पूर्व अभ्यास।
english: Again, (ones) bringing about special features of sattva (mind): the sattva of the mother and father, the repeated hearings of the pregnant woman; one's own accumulated action (karma) is, and past practice.

text_flags.why: satva is a spelling of sattva (normalised in words, also in mātāpitṛsatvāni); viśeṣa is correct as printed
possible: 'antairvatnyāḥ' for antarvatnyāḥ (pregnant woman); ar lost as ai
possible: final m lost; the comma is a print mark

notes: The sentence is a list of causes of the nature of the child's sattva; 'bhavati' (is) stands after karma and is translated literally; the sentence is not smoothed. sattva = mind, mental constitution (standard). śruti here = what is heard (hearing); it is not stated what is heard.
lines_deva: सत्वविशेषकराणि पुनर्मातापितृसत्वान्यंतैर्वत्न्याः श्रुतयश्चाभीक्ष्ण, स्वोपचितं कर्म भवति पूर्वाभ्यासश्चेति
lines_iast: satvaviśeṣakarāṇi punarmātāpitṛsatvānyaṃtairvatnyāḥ śrutayaścābhīkṣṇa, svopacitaṃ karma bhavati pūrvābhyāsaśceti

hindi: और इस विषय में होते हैं।
english: And in this matter there are (verses).
notes: Formula introducing the verses that follow; the noun 'verses' is not in the Sanskrit and is shown only in brackets.

hindi: घी, दूध आदि, मत्त्यासु नामक अस्पष्ट शब्द, प्रसन्न, कफ स्वभाव वालों में
english: Ghee, milk and the like, mattyāsu (unclear word), in cheerful (ones), in (ones) whose nature is Kapha

text_flags.why: possible: ā shortened before di; ghṛta-kṣīra-ādi
possible: damaged word; a form ending in -āsu (feminine locative plural) agreeing with muditāsu; not restored

notes: GROUPING: the sentence appears to continue in 158 ('the ārtava stays long'). The words ghṛta-kṣīra-ādi and mattyāsu are not joined into a firm sense: mattyāsu is damaged and is not interpreted. The feminine plural endings (muditāsu) show that women are meant, but the noun is not stated. The sentence appears to be completed in 158.

words.gloss: ārtava (menstrual blood, the female reproductive element; probable)

hindi: आर्तव यानी स्त्री का रज देर तक ठहरता है; विपरीतों में इससे अन्यथा।
english: The ārtava (menstrual blood, the female element) stays long; in the opposite (ones), otherwise than this.
notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 157. What the ārtava stays in is not stated. ārtava = menstrual blood / female reproductive fluid (probable; the text itself gives no more).

hindi: गिरने मात्र से ही रंग ग्रहण करता है, जैसे स्वच्छ वस्त्र।
english: From the mere falling (nipāta) it takes up colour, as a clean cloth does.
notes: The subject of gṛhṇāti is not stated (presumably the ārtava of 158 or the receiving element); not decided. 'nipāta' = falling (of the dye / of the fluid); not explained in the text.

hindi: निश्चित रूप से, अनुमानित पाठ पर गर्भ, वैसे ही बीज, क्षेत्र, तैयार किया हुआ बीज।
english: Certainly, on a conjectural reading the foetus, likewise the seed, the field, the prepared seed.

text_flags.why: possible: the s of garbhas lost before tathā; garbhaḥ tathā

notes: No verb; the line is elliptical and the connection between the terms is not stated. The field-and-seed pairing is the imagery of the tradition but the text here only lists the terms; no sense is built on it. dhruvam may be adverb 'certainly' or adjective 'sure' (agreeing with garbhaḥ). Review: upaskṛtam (n. sg.) could also agree with kṣetram and bījam together ('field and seed, prepared'); the translation keeps the plain list.

hindi: दैव के अविरुद्ध रहने पर, निश्चित रूप से, काल में, प्रयुक्त कर्म की
english: When fate (daiva) is unopposed, certainly, in time, of an applied action
notes: GROUPING: the sentence appears to continue in 162 ('siddhiḥ', success), so the subject 'success' is in the next unit. daiva = fate (what is due to previous action); not explained here.
lines_deva: अविरुद्धे ध्रुवं दैवे काले युक्तस्य कर्मणः
lines_iast: aviruddhe dhruvaṃ daive kāle yuktasya karmaṇaḥ

hindi: सिद्धि; इस कारण पुंसवन आदि को प्रकट होने से पहले प्रयोग में लाए।
english: Success; therefore one should apply puṃsavana and the like before manifestation.

text_flags.why: possible: final m lost

notes: GROUPING: appears to complete 161 (siddhiḥ). 'vyakteḥ' is the manifestation (of the foetus) as in 131; the foetus is not named in this unit. puṃsavana = rite for obtaining a male child (see 131). Review: puṃsavanādyasmāt is read puṃsavana-ādi + asmāt ('therefore'), not yasmāt.

hindi: और इस प्रकार जन्मे हुए रूपवान, महान् सत्त्व वाले और दीर्घायु होते हैं।
english: And those born thus are beautiful, of great sattva (mind), long-lived.
notes: No verb is stated (elliptical); the plural 'born (ones)' is read as people, since the following adjectives are masculine plural. rūpa = form/beauty.

hindi: अच्छे पुत्र ऋण से मुक्त कराने वाले हों, पुत्र वालों द्वारा माने गए।
english: Good sons would be releasers from debt, regarded by those who have sons.
notes: 'putriṇām matāḥ' is read as 'regarded (so) by those who have sons' (genitive of the agent with a past participle); the alternative 'accounted among those with sons' is possible. ṛṇa = debt; the kind of debt is not stated. Review: suputrāḥ is taken as the subject of syuḥ and matāḥ; the alternative division 'they would be releasers from debt; good sons are so regarded by those who have sons' needs a supplied subject and 'so'.

words.gloss: devoted to the gods, conduct, purity and the like

hindi: जो देवताओं, आचार, शौच आदि में रत है, वह महान् गुणों वाले को जन्म देती है।
english: She who is devoted to the gods, conduct, purity and the like bears (one) of great qualities.
notes: The noun 'woman' is understood from the feminine ratā and is not stated; 'one of great qualities' (child) is shown without a noun for the same reason. The compound is read 'devoted to (the worship of) gods, conduct, purity, etc.'; daivata may be taken with ācāra as 'conduct towards the gods'.

words.gloss: through connection with practice of a former birth

hindi: इसी प्रकार आचरण किया हुआ पूर्व जन्म के अभ्यास के योग से दौड़ता है।
english: In this way, and what is practised runs (dhāvati) through its connection with practice from a former birth.
notes: Word order is as printed: 'dhāvati evaṃ ca ācaritam'. dhāvati (runs, moves; also 'washes') is read as 'runs on / is carried on'; the sentence is hard and the sense is not made firm. prāgjanma = former birth (alternatively 'birth before'); not decided.

words.gloss: śukra (semen; here of women, so reproductive fluid)

hindi: स्त्रियाँ भी पुरुष के साथ समागम में शुक्र यानी प्रजनन द्रव का स्राव करती ही हैं।
english: Women too indeed discharge śukra (semen; here of women, the reproductive fluid) at union with a man.
notes: śukra is normally semen (standard); applied to women it is read as the reproductive fluid. 'puṃsaḥ samāgame' = 'at union with a man' (genitive with samāgama).

hindi: वह गर्भ के लिए कुछ भी नहीं करता, ऐसा नहीं सोचा जाता।
english: It is not thought that it does nothing at all for the foetus.
notes: 'That' is the śukra of 167. The double negation is as printed: 'tat garbhasya na kiñcit karoti' = it does nothing for the foetus; 'iti na cintyate' = this is not thought.
lines_deva: गर्भस्य तन्न किंचित्तु करोतीति न चिंत्यते
lines_iast: garbhasya tanna kiṃcittu karotīti na ciṃtyate

words.gloss: named Putrakāmīya (relating to the desire for a son)

hindi: इस प्रकार पुत्रकामीय नामक प्रथम अध्याय।
english: Thus the first chapter, named Putrakāmīya.
notes: Colophon. 'Putrakāmīya' = 'relating to the desire for a son'. The closing iti is a colophon marker.
